The other ten runs of the reproduction completed (state: /data/haiyangw/nrpic/scratch/E-stoch-inf/repro_scope_seq/state.tsv and seq.log). For each of the five: how far it got against its tlim (chain logs under <run dir>/chain/), whether its newest restart file is intact, and continue it to its end as a registered run that starts from that restart file with the same executable and input (Track F continued a run this way: tracks/F-hills/binary_conv/scripts/athena_resume_bc.sh on branch track/F-hills, a wrapper for the chain launcher of harness/bin/nrpic-run; write your own under repro/continue/scripts/), with segments enough to finish. Then wait for them (each needs an hour at most: poll with an until loop every five minutes, at most 150 minutes in all), close them (harness/bin/nrpic-run finish), and check that each continuation joins its original: same step, the records continue without a jump (the box is periodic, so the restart is exact: compare the first record after the restart with the last before it). HANDOFF.md as soon as the runs are submitted, updated when they end: per label the original run id, the continuation run id, the files, and how to read the two as one run (package repro/figs works beside you and reads it). If a run turns out broken and not merely cut, say so plainly. README.md; JOURNAL.md.

items.title: the figures of arXiv:2512.14649 from our runs

A lead session of this owner may be working in the worktree beside you: commit path-limited, only your package directory and your run manifests. PACKAGE repro/figs: every figure of arXiv:2512.14649 remade from our runs in the paper's layout and our style, and every analysis-only row of the map. Inputs: repro/scope/REPRO_MAP.md, HANDOFF.md (per figure: run ids, files, reader), SETUP_AUDIT.md, CARD_PLAN.md, JOURNAL.md entry 1 (predictions P1 to P7). First close the card runs of repro/scope that have ended (harness/bin/nrpic-run finish; actual costs into CARD_PLAN.md if its sequencer has not done so) and judge its predictions. Then, by registered analysis runs on processors (at most 6 cores; read 256-cell dumps one at a time): Fig. 1, the mean rolls at 64 cells (potential, first and second slow-roll parameter against e-folds, with the Friedmann solution) for both scenarios; Figs. 2 and 4, percentile contours (68, 95, 99, 100) against e-folds of the contrasts of the field, its momentum and the extrinsic curvature, of the reconstructed R, and of the constraints relative to their absolute magnitudes; Figs. 3 and 5, the binned dimensionless spectra of the reconstructed R against the linear solution from the initial to the final time (bins with more than ten modes; the band is the full range in a bin), panels as in the paper; Fig. 6, the spectra of the anisotropic sector for both scenarios; Fig. 7, the convergence of the spectrum; Fig. 8, the convergence of the constraints for both scenarios; Fig. 9, the ablation of the stochastic backreaction: from the runs of package repro/ablation (its HANDOFF.md: three levels for each scenario at 256 cells with the mode equation of the noise on the mesh, made with the executable of branch core/noise-level2; level 2 and level 1 are compared with level 0 on the mesh, coord/DECISIONS/0031), and beside it the level-1 runs of repro/scope against the released level 0; close the ablation runs that have ended (harness/bin/nrpic-run finish) and judge the predictions of repro/ablation/JOURNAL.md; a run that has not ended is marked pending with what reads it. For each figure: look at ours and at the paper's (open the paper's figure file in the store to look at it; never copy it), and write what agrees and by which measure, what differs and why, naming each of the four set-up differences of the audit where it matters. RESULTS.md: verdict per figure and per statement of the map (REPRODUCED, IN PART, NOT REPRODUCED, PENDING) with a ledger (number, run id, script). figures/ with scripts that a reader can rerun; README.md; JOURNAL.md with predictions before each analysis. Note on the state of the runs (2026-11-24): ten of the fifteen runs completed; five were cut by their segment limit (RSF256 = E-20261123-035925-8439d79, RNC256 = E-20261123-045030-c20bcb3, CL256U = E-20261123-065855-265732a, CL256S = E-20261123-090727-4b6e5a5 (package repro/scope, release executable of core-v0.6) and AL2S = E-20261123-152119-38957ba (package repro/ablation, branch executable of core/noise-level2; it reached t = 7.53 of 8.5)) and are being continued now by package repro/continue beside you: its HANDOFF.md names each continuation run and how to read it with its original as one run. Do first everything that needs only complete runs; then the figures that need the continued ones; if those have not ended when you need them, wait (until loop, five minutes, at most two hours) rather than leave a figure out.

Review, as the maintainer, of the diff of this branch (core/noise-level2, in this worktree) against main. It was written on Opus on 2026-11-22 because the weekly usage window did not hold a session on Fable (coord/DECISIONS/0029 item 2, 0031); it enters a release only after this review. Six source files, about 600 added lines, mostly athenak/src/scalar_field/scalar_field_noise_mesh.cpp; design note tracks/core/interfaces/noise_level2.md; tests and failed predictions in tracks/core/JOURNAL-noise-level2.md; Track E's card smoke check of the executable passed and its six ablation runs at 256 cells used the executable of commit 6ca93cba (tracks/E-stoch-inf/repro/ablation on branch track/E-stoch-inf). Check against the paper (/data/haiyangw/nrpic/kb-data/raw/arxiv/2512.14649/v2/src/PRD_v2.tex lines 220-323, 474-500, 697-713, 776-791) and by derivation: the well-posed form of the equation of R and its momentum; the local coefficients of level 2; the two readings the implementer marked as judgement (the paper's time derivative of the background field read as the normal derivative Pi; the Laplacian read as gamma^ij d_i d_j R without the connection term): decide which reading is right at the order the paper keeps and what the other would change; the background of the window at level 2; the normalisation of the projection as the adjoint of the synthesis; the stage coefficients of the low-storage RK4 for the new fields; restart; ghost exchange and boundary treatment of the new fields; the non-finite guard; correctness on the card (captures, races, host/device copies); cost (the recomputed V = Pi_R/Z in the projection). Run the branch's tests again and add one of your own where the review leaves a doubt (processors; at most half a card-hour if a card test is needed). Fix what is wrong, in small commits with tests. FIRST LINE of your report: either 'RESULTS UNCHANGED: the six ablation runs made with 6ca93cba stand' or 'RESULTS CHANGE: rerun the level-2 ablation', and in the second case publish the corrected executables under /data/haiyangw/nrpic/scratch/core/exe/core_noise-level2/ (new COMMIT, SHA256SUMS, READY) and tell Track E by an outbox message which runs to repeat. Verdict for release v0.7: fit, or the conditions that remain. Byte regression against release core-v0.6 with the options absent. Journal, interface text, commit, push.

Subject: the reproduction, in the papers' own set-up, of 'Stochastic Inflation in General Relativity' (arXiv:2401.08530) and 'Stochastic Inflation in Numerical Relativity' (arXiv:2512.14649): the lattice part with this repository's AthenaK (the Z4c system with an inflaton and stochastic sources), the one-patch Langevin part with a reference integrator. Rules of this program on top of the skill: every number has a ledger row with a run id or a source locator (tables/ledger, built by a script); data figures are made by registered scripts from raw outputs (copy the figure scripts of repro/figs and repro/langevin into manuscript/scripts/ and rerun them through one registered run_all); one schematic of the pipeline (harness/style/paperfig.py); the papers' figures are never copied. Follow the skill's procedure for a paper written from scratch (its section 10.1: the short versions first; reviewers as parallel subagents if this session can start them, otherwise say so), the voice pass (10.2), the checker, compile, and read every rendered page. Deliver manuscript/main.pdf and say in README.md how to rebuild it.

PACKAGE repro/verify: the fresh verifier of the reproduction. Trust nothing: do not read the READMEs' verdicts, RESULTS.md, the note's text or the journals before your own verdicts are committed (take from them only the list of claims and the locations of raw outputs). Predictions first. With short code of your own (readers of your own; the packages' readers only after a test on an analytic field): (1) arXiv:2401.08530: that the paper's background reaches the slope of its potential only with a forward Euler step of 0.01 e-folds and the converged background stops on the plateau; that its figures are matched by the Ito reading of the printed equations and not by the Stratonovich reading (decide from the paper's own figures by looking at them, and say how firmly); the factor of the Ito term (alpha^5 against the printed alpha^3) by a derivation and a Monte Carlo test of your own; the noise amplitude of appendix D in slow roll and ultra-slow roll against your own solution of the mode equation. (2) arXiv:2512.14649: from the raw dumps of the 256-cell runs, the spectrum of the reconstructed R against the linear solution per mode and per bin at the final time for both scenarios; the freezing of R; the constraint ratios and their absolute magnitudes; the sign-flip control; the difference between backreaction levels; two numbers of the convergence figures; the slow-roll parameters at the final time. (3) A sample of six of the seventeen misprints of repro/equations/ERRATA.md, each rederived. (4) Every number of the note's ledger that you did not cover above, by rerunning its script, and ten of them from raw outputs. VERIFIER.md: what was checked and how, per claim CONFIRMED, NOT CONFIRMED or WRONG with the evidence, what could not be checked, the three weakest points of the reproduction. Registered runs; figures looked at.
